claim: How MTD is measured to perform depends on how the attacker is implemented.
quote: Attack and defense efforts vary depending on the imposed threat.
issue: Hong says MTD effort/effectiveness varies with the threat type, and that comparing MTD needs knowledge of attacker capabilities (p. 34). He does not say measured values depend on how an attacker is implemented in a simulation; his own response is metrics computed from network changes, 'instead of against individual attack instances' (Sec. 3.1). Right direction, wider than the source; Hong is the supervisor.
fix_text: "depends on how the attacker is implemented [hong2018]" -> "depends on the attacker it faces [hong2018]"

claim: ASP, MTTC and NCR are computed from what the attacker does, so their values depend on how the attacker is implemented.
quote: This approach simplifies the attack model that only requires their characteristics, in comparison to enlisting all possible attack instances.
issue: Hong discusses none of ASP, MTTC or NCR (NCR is Zhang's), and his metrics are computed from the graphical model, not from attacker actions. The source carries only the general point (efforts vary with the threat, Sec. 3); the 'computed from what the attacker does, so ...' step is the dissertation's own reasoning.
fix_text: "so their values depend on how the attacker is implemented [hong2018]" -> "so their values depend on how the attacker is implemented, as MTD effectiveness depends on the threat [hong2018]"

claim: Attack path variation, number and exposure are attacker-side effectiveness metrics.
quote: the attack path variation (APV) measures the shift in attack paths as the network changes when MTD techniques are deployed ... The APE metric measures the amount of attack path exposure for all network states.
issue: Hong groups APV, APN and APE as reconnaissance attack-effort metrics for MTD effectiveness (APN, Sec. 5.1.2, p. 40); attacker-side follows Cho's frame.

claim: Distinct openings is the dissertation's metric, after Hong.
quote: That is, APV captures the change in the set of attack paths between the network states.
issue: 'After' is honest: APV measures change in a network's attack paths across MTD states, distinct openings counts variety in one attacker's openings across runs, different objects; the prose (U0539-U0540) states the difference. Equation label eq:apv is a leftover name only.

claim: Hong et al. measure how much the attack paths (sequences of hosts) change when an MTD deployment changes the network.
quote: the attack path variation (APV) measures the shift in attack paths as the network changes when MTD techniques are deployed
issue: Attack paths are on the HARM upper layer, 'an Attack Graph that captures only the reachability of hosts that establishes attack paths' (p. 37, Def. 2), so 'sequences of hosts' holds. Six authors, 'et al.' correct.

claim: Metric values depend on how the attacker is implemented.
quote: Attack and defense efforts vary depending on the imposed threat.
issue: Hong says MTD effort/effectiveness varies with the threat type, and that comparing MTD needs knowledge of attacker capabilities (p. 34). He does not say measured values depend on how an attacker is implemented in a simulation; his own response is metrics computed from network changes, 'instead of against individual attack instances' (Sec. 3.1). Right direction, wider than the source; Hong is the supervisor. Same claim as U0211, restated.
fix_text: "metric values depend on how the attacker is implemented [hong2018]" -> "metric values depend on the attacker [hong2018]"
